purpose: TH-SEARCH-R1-018 spec section 20: re-run the R1-017 parent-vs-specialist differential for the three hubs that received fixes (Move, Insurance, Contractor) and confirm the ask surface and each specialist's own direct contract still agree semantically post-fix.
method: For every corpus entry tagged testSurfaces including both 'ask' and 'direct' for move/insurance/contractor, compare the ask-surface result (via orchestrateGuidedResearch, specialist-execution/v2 contract) against the direct-surface result (each specialist's own public API/page, its native contract).

cases.note: Exact identifier lookup; both surfaces resolve to the same single record.

Both surfaces correctly report zero matching rows for this disputed/under-review MC association (see identifierIntegrity note on JK Moving), not a false zero -- consistent with the count/false-zero audit.

This is the same pre-existing dual-contract architecture noted throughout R1-005/006/014/016/017: the direct move-ask-v1 contract (lib/move-ask/*, the older R1-005-certified conservative distinctiveTokens() candidate-name-search path) intentionally surfaces a broader slate of source-backed name candidates (5, including token-prefix and distinctive-legal-name-token hits like 'JK Brokerage Services' and 'JK Van Lines') for human review, each individually disclosed with its own nameMatchEvidence/rank/whyMatched. The ask surface goes through specialist-execution/v2 (lib/search/*), which after the R1-018 similarHit() fix now applies a *stricter* identity-tier match and returns only the 2 highest-confidence identities. The parent surface is intentionally narrower/safer than the direct candidate-browse surface, not wider -- this is the correct direction and is exactly what BLOCKER-MOVE-01's fix was intended to produce. No semantic disagreement: both surfaces are internally consistent with their own documented match-confidence contracts, and the parent never claims a false precision the specialist doesn't also support.

Different query MODE, not a data disagreement: the direct move-ask-v1 contract classifies a bare geography+move-type phrase as a MOVE_JOURNEY definitional/research-guidance query (resultType:'definition', returning a checklist and state-authority capability pointer, zero company rows by design -- this is its documented 'journey research' behavior, unrelated to BLOCKER-MOVE-01 and untouched by the R1-018 fix). The ask surface's specialist-execution/v2 contract instead treats the same phrase as a geography-scoped cohort search and returns actual candidate rows (267). This is a pre-existing grain/mode difference between the two Move contracts (journey-definition vs cohort-search), not a regression introduced by R1-018, and is consistent with the 'HQ != service territory' and general definition/cohort separation documented in the R1-017 source-grain audit.
Confirms the IDENTIFIER-FILLER-WORD-01 fix: 'NAIC code 10064' now parses identically to a bare 'NAIC 10064' on both surfaces.

Confirms BLOCKER-INSURANCE-01 fix: the parent now correctly fails closed to a directory handoff instead of fabricating an 82071-row unscoped cohort; the direct specialist agrees this capability is unsupported.

Confirms BLOCKER-CONTRACTOR-01 fix: the ask surface now reaches the specialist (contractFingerprint check relaxed) and returns the same 924-row Broward roofer cohort the direct specialist page shows; both surfaces agree the request is supported.

summary.verdict: PASS -- every comparable Move/Insurance/Contractor case either agrees exactly between the ask and direct surfaces, or diverges for a pre-existing, already-understood architectural reason (dual Move contracts; journey-definition vs cohort-search mode) unrelated to and unchanged by the R1-018 fixes. No new or unexplained parent/specialist disagreement was introduced.
